title: O Lord of Hosts, Whose Glory Fills
description: O Lord of Hosts, Whose Glory Fills in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Mason Neale wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 450.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord of hosts, whose glo-ry fills The bounds of the e-ter-nal hills And yet vouch-saf’st, in Chris-tian lands, To dwell in tem-ples made with hands;

lines: O Lord of hosts, whose glory fills
The bounds of the eternal hills
And yet vouchsaf’st, in Christian lands,
To dwell in temples made with hands;
Grant that all we who here to-day
May be in very deed Thine own,
The heads that guide endue with skill,
The hands that work preserve from ill,
That we, who these foundations lay
May raise the top-stone in its day.
But now and ever, Lord, protect
The temple of Thine own elect;
Be Thou in them and they in Thee,

licence: Public domain: John Mason Neale died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Mason Neale (1818–1866), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
